caption: What if you were a bird on a power line? Many street wires in India carry 11,000 volts, almost 50 times the 230 volts in your home socket, yet a pigeon can sit there all day. Electricity only flows when there is a voltage difference, and both of the bird's feet are on the same wire at the same voltage, so almost no current passes through it. Touch a second wire, or the wire and the pole, and current rushes through the body. That is why big birds with wide wings are at risk: WWF-India counted more than 130 vultures and eagles electrocuted on just 4 km of lines near Dehradun between 2014 and 2019. Covering those wires fixed it, with no deaths recorded there since 2025. Plot twist: trained linemen in metal-thread suits work on live lines the same way. Never try it, never touch any wire, and never pull a kite off one. Did YOU know why birds are safe? 👇
